findings.reason: as written the guard is evaluated against a run id that does not yet name the request, so a node implementing it literally leaves an orphan `steering.md` per re-dispatch and the "must never overwrite" rule is satisfied only by accident; the fix is to resolve the request's id before the copy (the caller at dispatch.py:1733 already holds `existing["run_id"]`) or move the copy after dedup in `reckon/crew/runs.py`, which is not among §5's declared write paths.
findings.text: §5 makes `_queued_request_record` (dispatch.py:229) copy `--brief` into `steering.md` "only when the request's run directory holds no `steering.md` yet", and says that guard is what stops an in-place re-queue overwriting an edit; but on that arm the builder is called at dispatch.py:1733 with the new dispatch's `run_id`, and the identity match that finds the existing request happens afterwards inside `queue_dispatch` (runs.py:576-584), which then rewrites `record["run_id"] = existing_run_id` (runs.py:616). The directory the builder would test and write is therefore `run_dir(<fresh-id>)`, always empty of `steering.md`, not the queue's `run_dir(<existing-id>)` — so the guard never sees the edited file, the original `--brief` is copied into an orphan run directory that no pointer names, and the done-when's third arm still passes because launch reads the existing directory.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every code anchor in §5 resolves (`_queued_request_record` `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:229`, `_launch_queued`/`_node_from_pointer` `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:171`/`:119`, `_store_brief`/`_brief_digest` `reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:2241`/`:2204`, `reckon/mcp_crew_actions.py`), and each plan href resolves to an existing `docs/plans/*.html` target.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §5's six arms include a declared negative control (the discriminating arm that leaves `steering.md` alone and changes the pointer's brief, which fails on today's copy-at-dispatch code) plus refusal arms for a launched request, an undeclared model and an invalid steering file.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §5 keeps every log under the request's own run directory (`~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<request-id>/`, `runs_dir()` in `reckon/crew/runs.py:79`), and §14 writes to `docs/evidence/archive/a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan-landed.html`; nothing lands in a scratchpad or node-local `/tmp`.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5 introduces `steering.md` and `crew queue edit|reprioritise|drop`, all named by what they do; no plan label, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §5 says the copy guard is evaluated inside `_queued_request_record` against "the request's run directory", but on the in-place re-queue arm that builder is handed the re-dispatch's fresh run id, which `queue_dispatch` rewrites to the existing request's id only afterwards.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 is one deliverable (a brief that binds at launch and stays editable until then); the two-node build split is explicitly allowed inside the section and each node's share is named.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5's declared `depends-on: [s2]` holds, and every consumer of its verbs (`s4`, and `s10`/`s13`/`s15` through `s4`) is transitively ordered after it; the one external edge (`s14` on `imas-ambix:local-lane-admission-control#s27`) is declared in the direction the plan states.
